person-001.name: Avery Brooks
person-001.bio: I work the front desk at the clinic in Hayward. Come August, there's usually a bag of zucchini on my desk for whoever will take it.

person-002.name: Jasmine Carter
person-002.bio: I fix water mains around Jackson. Still trying to play nine holes without losing a ball.

person-003.name: Emily Mercer
person-003.bio: I teach grown-ups to swim. The best part is when someone lets go of the wall and forgets to be nervous.

person-004.name: Angela Nguyen
person-004.bio: I look at other people's leaky windows for a living. Mine's on the list, I promise.

person-005.name: Grace Patel
person-005.bio: I write the live captions at shows. My favorite nights are the ones when I can feel the audience laughing behind me.

person-006.name: Caroline Price
person-006.bio: Most of my workday is little bottles of well water. My camera roll is mostly pictures of the drive home.

person-007.name: Maya Washington
person-007.bio: I spend a lot of mornings looking for tracks along the road. If you've got a good Wyoming author to recommend, I'm listening.

person-008.name: Isabel Rivera
person-008.bio: I make dulcimers in a shared shop. Come by on game night and you can usually hear somebody tuning one between turns.

person-009.name: Rachel Kim
person-009.bio: If you have an old sewing machine that won't run, I probably want to see it. Especially if it still has the foot pedal.

person-010.name: Zoe Sanders
person-010.bio: I draw tiny pixel characters for games. The walk cycle always takes me longer than drawing the whole little guy.

person-011.name: Elijah Reed
person-011.bio: I coach the school debate team. On the weekends I like a long walk with absolutely no stopwatch.

person-012.name: Marcus Green
person-012.bio: I groom ski trails before most folks are up. By movie night I'm lucky if I make it past the opening credits.

person-013.name: Noah Bennett
person-013.bio: I'm the one who brings bread to pickup basketball. Nobody's complained about that arrangement yet.

person-014.name: Caleb Foster
person-014.bio: I give tours in Savannah and grow herbs on my steps. Ask me which one's mint before you brush past it.

person-015.name: Isaac Turner
person-015.bio: My idea of a nice evening is getting an old game console to boot. I spend enough of the day fixing other people's dishwashers.

person-016.name: Julian Hart
person-016.bio: I'm on the road visiting farms most of the week. I know which gyms in the area have a good Friday night game.

person-017.name: Micah Allen
person-017.bio: I work in a ski shop in Salida. I own more pictures of the mountain at sunrise than pictures of myself skiing it.

person-018.name: Andre Walker
person-018.bio: I pick movies for a little theater in Alpine. Tell me about a movie you wish you'd seen on the big screen.

person-019.name: Lucas Hayes
person-019.bio: I schedule small planes in Bethel. I keep something simmering on weather-delay days because dinner's about the only thing I can predict.

person-020.name: Devin Miller
person-020.bio: I film local sports. I still get excited when a kid spots themselves in a replay for the first time.

person-021.name: Valeria Cortés
person-021.bio: I'm usually at the produce stand in Selma. The first good peaches of the season are worth getting sticky for.

person-022.name: Ximena Salgado
person-022.bio: I get called out when a pump quits. I keep a camera in the truck because the light out here can be ridiculous.

person-023.name: Elena Pineda
person-023.bio: I plant rain gardens around Tacoma. At home there's usually an unfinished board game taking up the kitchen table.

person-024.name: Renata Lozano
person-024.bio: I take care of a park by the water. I know a surprising number of the regulars by their dogs' names.

person-025.name: Camila Ibarra
person-025.bio: I help out at the skate park and feed whoever's still there when I fire up the grill.

person-026.name: Lucía Meza
person-026.bio: I work with kids at an elementary school. I set alarms for meteor showers and sometimes even get out of bed for them.

person-027.name: Marisol Vega
person-027.bio: I work on buses in Cleveland. Fall Sundays are for football and whatever I can eat off a paper plate.

person-028.name: Adriana Peña
person-028.bio: I keep the trains powered up. Most Thursday nights I'm at a friend's place rolling dice and taking the scenic route through a dungeon.

person-029.name: Sofía Treviño
person-029.bio: I teach people to grow things they can eat. My favorite question is what to do with all the basil.

person-030.name: Daniela Montes
person-030.bio: I look after sheet music for our orchestra. I bring home concert programs from every trip and never know where to put them.

person-031.name: Diego Olvera
person-031.bio: I find a kitchen for food that would otherwise get tossed. My dog takes a keen interest in the unloading process.

person-032.name: Mateo Barrera
person-032.bio: I spend a lot of Saturdays down by the stream in Dillon. I've usually got mud on me somewhere.

person-033.name: Iván Aranda
person-033.bio: I build things for a children's museum. The real test is handing something to a roomful of six-year-olds.

person-034.name: Raúl Córdova
person-034.bio: I open a coffee shop in Decorah. By kickoff I've already been up long enough to call nachos dinner.

person-035.name: Sergio Robles
person-035.bio: I mend fences and listen to audiobooks between jobs. Happy to trade recommendations for anything with a good narrator.

person-036.name: Arturo Castañeda
person-036.bio: I live in Hilo and spend a lot of time tracking down appliance parts. If there's football on I'm easy to find.

person-037.name: Nicolás Ríos
person-037.bio: I run a small salon in Savannah. Half my regulars have known me long enough to remember my own questionable haircuts.

person-038.name: Andrés Peralta
person-038.bio: I plan snow routes in Fargo. First snowfall still makes me reach for the camera, even when it also means I'm on call.

person-039.name: Luis Becerra
person-039.bio: I set climbing routes. There's usually a paperback and a roll of finger tape at the bottom of my bag.

person-040.name: Emilio Zamora
person-040.bio: I work with hospice families around Abingdon. I keep a pair of basketball shoes in the car for pickup games on the way home.

person-041.name: Mariana Moreira
person-041.bio: I get internet out to houses around West Plains. My friends know exactly who to call when game night starts lagging.

person-042.name: Tainá Nascimento
person-042.bio: I'm at the pharmacy most weekdays. At home I'm slowly figuring out which repairs I can do without a second trip to the hardware store.

person-043.name: Beatriz Rocha
person-043.bio: I grow native plants for restoration projects. My windowsills are nearly as crowded as the greenhouse.

person-044.name: Luana Ribeiro
person-044.bio: I teach sewing in Paintsville. I made my own apron and immediately got tomato sauce all over it.

person-045.name: Paula Andrade
person-045.bio: I teach new folks around a machine shop. Away from work I paint tiny figures for game night, usually with more enthusiasm than precision.

person-046.name: Aline Duarte
person-046.bio: I take library books out into the community. If there's an old Portland photo with no street name on it, I want a look.

person-047.name: Júlia Nunes
person-047.bio: I check auto parts in Detroit and play golf when I can. I keep finding tees in my work pants.

person-048.name: Renata Queiroz
person-048.bio: I organize a hockey league. Come summer I like a trail that doesn't involve a schedule or a sign-up sheet.

person-049.name: Ana Luísa Barros
person-049.bio: I make community radio in Worcester. I also host board game nights, so talking people through the rules is kind of a second job.

person-050.name: Isabela Teixeira
person-050.bio: I fix instruments in Pittsburgh. I'm always happy to hear how an old guitar ended up in somebody's family.

person-051.name: Rafael Almeida
person-051.bio: I'm the person counting lunch trays at school. I play co-op games in the evenings if anybody needs one more.

person-052.name: Thiago Pinto
person-052.bio: I bake out of my kitchen in Galesburg. I try to photograph the good batches before someone cuts the first slice.

person-053.name: João Pedro Castro
person-053.bio: I work behind the scenes at a maritime museum. I can lose a whole lunch break reading a sailor's old letters.

person-054.name: Daniel Gomes
person-054.bio: I call cues at the local theater. During basketball season I try very hard to keep my phone off backstage.

person-055.name: Gabriel Reis
person-055.bio: I restore old granite. When I travel, half my photos end up being close-ups of stonework.

person-056.name: Leandro Machado
person-056.bio: I teach safety on a warehouse floor in Memphis. Most weekends you can find me helping somebody move something heavy.

person-057.name: Felipe Silveira
person-057.bio: I help get beach wheelchairs down to the water. I'm usually still finding sand in my shoes by the time I get to the golf course.

person-058.name: Victor Cardoso
person-058.bio: I organize school meal deliveries. Morning light on the way out of Winslow is what got me into photography.

person-059.name: Caio Farias
person-059.bio: I teach computer classes at the community center. Bring me your list of questions. I like the handwritten ones best.

person-060.name: Bruno Azevedo
person-060.bio: I volunteer on fire lookout near Burns. A thermos and a comfortable chair go a long way on a quiet shift.

person-061.name: Milagros Vidal
person-061.bio: I'm a paramedic in Pittsburgh. I'll happily play a slow round of golf with anyone who's up for carrying their own snacks.

person-062.name: Abril Mansilla
person-062.bio: I tape ankles for school teams. I take pictures on the sidelines when I've got a free hand.

person-063.name: Julieta Rivas
person-063.bio: I drive between home health visits around Mountain View. Library audiobooks get me through the long stretches.

person-064.name: Malena Pereyra
person-064.bio: I look after rain gauges around Hilo. You'd think I'd remember an umbrella more often.

person-065.name: Josefina Acosta
person-065.bio: I order supplies for a hospital. At home I'm forever trying to fit one more shelf into the garage.

person-066.name: Catalina Leiva
person-066.bio: I rebuild big pumps in Price. On a good Saturday I get the tools put away in time to walk nine holes.

person-067.name: Pilar Santoro
person-067.bio: I run our adult softball league. I've got a camera full of people diving for balls they had no chance of catching.

person-068.name: Rocío Ferreyra
person-068.bio: I plan hospital maintenance in Marquette. I like fixing things with people, especially when there are doughnuts involved.

person-069.name: Martina Ponce
person-069.bio: I install storm shelters around Woodward. Fall weekends usually find me under a blanket in the bleachers.

person-070.name: Agustina Gaitán
person-070.bio: I deliver bread by bike in Durham. You can usually tell where I've been by the smell of my jacket.

person-071.name: Santiago Arce
person-071.bio: I help arrange rides in Paintsville. Give me an old street name and I can probably tell you what it is now.

person-072.name: Lautaro Quiroga
person-072.bio: I run a childcare center and live with a very opinionated cat. They're two different kinds of patience.

person-073.name: Tomás Molina
person-073.bio: I drive for a food pantry in Fort Wayne. I've gotten pretty good at getting one more box into a full van.

person-074.name: Bautista Ocampo
person-074.bio: I volunteer on stream cleanups. Afterwards I make a pot of chili big enough for anyone who wants to stick around.

person-075.name: Emiliano Luna
person-075.bio: I work in the woods around Elkins. My dog still acts like the short walk after work is the day's main event.

person-076.name: Franco Sosa
person-076.bio: I teach agriculture. I can usually get a class talking by asking what went wrong in the greenhouse over the weekend.

person-077.name: Joaquín Roldán
person-077.bio: I interpret for folks around El Paso. My best tomatoes grow in the one corner of the yard I almost didn't plant.

person-078.name: Matías Ledesma
person-078.bio: I work in an archive in New Haven. I'm the friend who turns over an old photograph hoping somebody wrote the date.

person-079.name: Ramiro Herrera
person-079.bio: I volunteer on the museum train in Ely. I'm happiest when a kid asks enough questions to make us both learn something.

person-080.name: Facundo Rivero
person-080.bio: I grow baby shellfish in Cedar Key. I learned a few constellations on early shifts and keep meaning to learn a few more.

person-081.name: Nora Sinclair
person-081.bio: I look after railroad signals in Newark. On my days off I check on my peppers before I've even made coffee.

person-082.name: Élodie Fortin
person-082.bio: I coordinate buses for the school band. If anybody finds a lone black dress shoe after a trip, I probably know its owner.

person-083.name: Céline Bergeron
person-083.bio: I teach music at a few different schools. There's almost always a tambourine or a board game rattling around in my car.

person-084.name: Amara Clarke
person-084.bio: My day job involves spreadsheets. At home I measure garlic by what feels right and then add a little more.

person-085.name: Sophie MacLeod
person-085.bio: I keep the water running at a distillery in Louisville. My bedside stack of books is getting a bit out of hand.

person-086.name: Alina Park
person-086.bio: I work the freight dock in Billings. I come home smelling like cardboard and my dog investigates every pocket.

person-087.name: Margot Bouchard
person-087.bio: I fix heating systems around Berlin. A snow day with a book is my favorite kind of day off, when the phone cooperates.

person-088.name: Lily Chen
person-088.bio: I help people find housing in Long Beach. Show me a picture of your pet and we'll have plenty to talk about.

person-089.name: Nadia Desjardins
person-089.bio: I work the meat counter in Wichita. I keep binoculars by the back door for clear nights.

person-090.name: Mina Singh
person-090.bio: I build sets for a youth theater. My favorite photos are the ones where you can see the kids peeking out from the wings.

person-091.name: Owen Campbell
person-091.bio: I ref soccer and play board games. At least at game night I get to put the whistle away.

person-092.name: Louis Gagnon
person-092.bio: I work out on the ramp at the airport in Alpine. Back home there's always something in pieces on my workbench.

person-093.name: Marc Beaulieu
person-093.bio: I keep track of food shipments in Honolulu. Tell me what you've been listening to lately. My commute playlist needs help.

person-094.name: Ethan McKenzie
person-094.bio: I plow snow in North Adams. I know which of my neighbors will have a pot of coffee on at four in the morning.

person-095.name: Hugo Lévesque
person-095.bio: I fix drainage pumps around New Orleans. Taking apart a broken fan on the porch still counts as relaxing in my book.

person-096.name: Adrian Wu
person-096.bio: I work in a small hospital lab. I'm partial to the sort of video game I can pause when the kettle boils.

person-097.name: Kieran Fraser
person-097.bio: I roast coffee in Burlington. On Sundays I make pancakes and usually burn the one I'm supposed to eat.

person-098.name: Simon Pelletier
person-098.bio: I retired from aircraft inspection in Wichita. These days I get to spend an afternoon figuring out a game just because I feel like it.

person-099.name: Reid Martin
person-099.bio: I make tools in Cookeville. I grew up listening to football on the radio and still like it that way.

person-100.name: Amir Abbas
person-100.bio: I take water samples in the harbor. If I'm lucky, there's enough daylight left afterwards for a bucket of balls.

person-101.name: Imogen Shaw
person-101.bio: I teach preschool in Madison. A four-year-old gave me a bean in a paper cup and now I have a whole vegetable bed.

person-102.name: Leila Hussain
person-102.bio: I'm the one dragging the hose around the community garden. Come say hi if you see me trying to untangle it again.

person-103.name: Aisha Owen
person-103.bio: I help run a warming center in Duluth. I learned to fix a zipper there and now everyone brings me their coats.

person-104.name: Harriet Wood
person-104.bio: I own a bike shop in Lewisburg. My favorite customers are the kids who ride past the window to show me the repair held.

person-105.name: Alice Atkinson
person-105.bio: I fix food trucks around El Paso. My dog knows which stops sometimes come with a little piece of brisket.

person-106.name: Phoebe Clarke
person-106.bio: I weld for the city. I like taking pictures of Duluth just before the rest of the neighborhood wakes up.

person-107.name: Hannah MacDonald
person-107.bio: I run a game café. If you've got half an hour and have never played anything, I've got a shelf just for you.

person-108.name: Freya Hughes
person-108.bio: I work in a shared woodshop. I made a stand for my telescope and promptly spent the first clear night adjusting the legs.

person-109.name: Poppy Martin
person-109.bio: I service equipment on poultry farms. I stop for pictures on the drive home, which explains the dust on my camera.

person-110.name: Zara Davies
person-110.bio: I work on traffic signals in Boise. I like street photography, especially when somebody's dog wanders into the shot.

person-111.name: Callum Reid
person-111.bio: I work with growers in Orangeburg. Ask me about the garden after the game, unless you have a picture of a really strange bug.

person-112.name: Rhys Morgan
person-112.bio: I do payroll on a farm. My kitchen table doubles as a workbench more often than I'd like to admit.

person-113.name: Oliver Webb
person-113.bio: I buy used records for a shop in Eugene. Tell me what you played until the grooves wore out.

person-114.name: Rory Ellis
person-114.bio: I change tires all over Moultrie. I keep a notebook of lunch spots on my route and a separate page for the really good pie.

person-115.name: Samuel Watson
person-115.bio: I work in a biotech lab. On Fridays I like a game with a big map, lots of pieces and somebody else teaching the rules.

person-116.name: Tariq Ali
person-116.bio: I volunteer at the vet clinic. I also collect old postcards of Dodge City, preferably the ones somebody actually wrote on.

person-117.name: Finley Cooper
person-117.bio: I play piano for a gospel choir. After rehearsal I like to sit outside a few minutes while my ears stop ringing.

person-118.name: Ewan Scott
person-118.bio: I help community college students untangle financial aid forms. My idea of a Friday night is a matinee that turns into a double feature.

person-119.name: Nathan Ahmed
person-119.bio: I'm a nurse in Selma and help care for family at home. I love a story that starts with what used to be on that corner.
person-119.occupation: Rural clinic nurse and family caregiver

person-120.name: Toby Baker
person-120.bio: I teach lifeguards at the rec center. Funny enough, my favorite way to spend a day off is still at the water.

person-121.name: Manon Lefèvre
person-121.bio: I build guitars in Sandpoint. I love when somebody plays the first chord on one and immediately forgets I'm in the room.

person-122.name: Sarah Benali
person-122.bio: I used to look after the courthouse in Silver City. Now I fuss over my tomatoes with about the same attention to detail.

person-123.name: Léa Laurent
person-123.bio: I do trail work around Putnam. My dog considers inspecting every new footbridge a personal responsibility.

person-124.name: Amel Haddad
person-124.bio: I coach a robotics club after school. Some of our best afternoons start with a wheel falling off.

person-125.name: Camille Girard
person-125.bio: I deliver packages around Burns. A really good audiobook can make me look forward to the longest road on the route.

person-126.name: Chloé Robin
person-126.bio: I help apartment buildings go solar in Honolulu. At home the best patch of sunlight already belongs to the cat.

person-127.name: Inès Bensaïd
person-127.bio: I cook for a childcare center. Give me a day off and I'll pack lunch and go find somewhere to eat it outside.

person-128.name: Émilie Caron
person-128.bio: I prepare taxes in Cookeville. Once April's over I invite everyone back to my place for board games.

person-129.name: Maëlle Perrot
person-129.bio: I teach sea kayaking out of Port Angeles. I still get a kick out of watching someone steer through their first little swell.

person-130.name: Amandine Roy
person-130.bio: I dispatch bike deliveries in Tucson. I like comparing old street maps with the routes we actually ride.

person-131.name: Mathis Fontaine
person-131.bio: I'm a physical therapist in Worcester. I like long walks through neighborhoods where someone remembers the old shop names.

person-132.name: Hugo Moreau
person-132.bio: I volunteer on evacuation routes near Grass Valley. I'm the person with the folded paper map in the glove box.

person-133.name: Adam Belkacem
person-133.bio: I tutor adults in St. Johnsbury. I'm learning to bake bread myself, so I get plenty of practice being the beginner.

person-134.name: Noé Garcia
person-134.bio: I run the projector at film festivals. My cat has a perfect record of picking the quietest scene to ask for dinner.

person-135.name: Rémi Giraud
person-135.bio: I run the board at a radio station in Bethel. I'll take a crack at fixing just about anything with a loose knob.

person-136.name: Jules Mercier
person-136.bio: I do billing in a dental office. My favorite part of game night is the five minutes when everyone thinks they're winning.

person-137.name: Bastien Colin
person-137.bio: I help with programs at the library in Thibodaux. Show up for a meteor shower and I'll share my blanket.

person-138.name: Sami Gérard
person-138.bio: I teach in a library makerspace. I'm a sucker for movies where you can tell someone built the monster by hand.

person-139.name: Théo Blanc
person-139.bio: I drive refrigerated freight. If a rest stop has a decent walking trail, it goes straight into my notebook.

person-140.name: Léo Marchand
person-140.bio: I keep books for a hotel in Cape May. After the summer rush, the first quiet Sunday with a game on feels like a holiday.

person-141.name: Zofia Lis
person-141.bio: I inspect food truck kitchens around Boise. I try very hard not to read the game rules out loud in my work voice.

person-142.name: Alicja Kowalska
person-142.bio: I grow vegetables for a farm stand in Athens. I like hearing what people make with the things I bring.

person-143.name: Emilia Mazur
person-143.bio: I work on boats in Thibodaux. When it pours all weekend, I get a lot further in whatever game I'm playing.

person-144.name: Karolina Grabowska
person-144.bio: I help neighbors talk things out in Wilmington. I'm embarrassingly easy to win over with a good old movie.

person-145.name: Agata Król
person-145.bio: I take care of objects in a small Baltimore museum. My own board game boxes are held together with much less ceremony.

person-146.name: Julia Wójcik
person-146.bio: I repair backup generators in Ely. I've got a drawer labeled “might fit something” and it occasionally proves me right.

person-147.name: Marta Szymańska
person-147.bio: I plan bus routes in Dodge City. I'm up early enough to catch the bright planets before the sun comes up.

person-148.name: Anna Zielińska
person-148.bio: I spend workdays figuring out where the power went out. Most Saturdays I help at the community center, where the coffee is better.

person-149.name: Nina Pawlak
person-149.bio: I build cabinets and have a soft spot for old houses. You can learn a lot about a kitchen from the drawer everybody wears out first.

person-150.name: Iga Wróbel
person-150.bio: I work in the ER. After a long shift, give me a comfy seat and a movie I've already seen.

person-151.name: Jakub Kaczmarek
person-151.bio: I test games for accessibility. When I travel, I like finding the little arcade that somehow still has my favorite machine.

person-152.name: Adam Nowak
person-152.bio: I do lights for community theater. If a rehearsal runs late, I've usually got a paperback tucked in by the board.

person-153.name: Oskar Kamiński
person-153.bio: I look at insurance claims for work. Give me a clear night and I'd much rather look through a telescope.

person-154.name: Marek Dąbrowski
person-154.bio: I work in peer support around Elkins. If I really like a book, I'll buy another copy so I can lend it out.

person-155.name: Filip Zając
person-155.bio: I record oral histories in Selma. The good stuff often starts after somebody says, “Oh, you don't want to hear about that.”

person-156.name: Jan Górski
person-156.bio: I survey routes in Aurora. Old photos of the same streets are my favorite way to see what's changed.

person-157.name: Antoni Sokołowski
person-157.bio: I tend a university greenhouse. I have a playlist long enough to water the whole place, even on a hot day.

person-158.name: Kamil Kalinowski
person-158.bio: I buy coffee in Richmond. Lately I've been trying to grow enough mint for tea, which turns out to be the opposite problem.

person-159.name: Michał Wilk
person-159.bio: I run a school cafeteria. I like video games where I can put my feet up after a whole day of standing.

person-160.name: Piotr Jankowski
person-160.bio: I handle payroll for a school district. I fold dumplings when I want to do something with my hands after all those numbers.

person-161.name: Adaeze Nwosu
person-161.bio: I set type at a print shop in Milwaukee. I usually have a little ink under my nails, even on the golf course.

person-162.name: Amina Bello
person-162.bio: I put up shade structures in Tucson. My favorite part of a volunteer build is the first lunch underneath one.

person-163.name: Ifeoma Okeke
person-163.bio: I keep things working at the ferry terminal in Port Angeles. On days off I head for the trails above the water.

person-164.name: Zainab Ibrahim
person-164.bio: I help people figure out where the cold air gets into their houses. In a Baltimore rowhouse it can be quite a hunt.

person-165.name: Temilade Afolayan
person-165.bio: I fix refrigeration equipment in Buffalo. I'll take a spot in a pickup basketball game, even if you just need a fifth.

person-166.name: Chidinma Eze
person-166.bio: I dispatch trucks at the port. I've got more pictures of my dog asleep than of just about anything in Savannah.

person-167.name: Aisha Abubakar
person-167.bio: I inspect bridges around Pittsburgh. I love playing nine with people who don't mind stopping to look at the river.

person-168.name: Oluwaseun Ajayi
person-168.bio: I help run rec programs in Milford. The outdoor movie nights are my favorite, especially when everyone brings a lawn chair.

person-169.name: Nneka Umeh
person-169.bio: I'm an electrician in Manchester. I spend an unreasonable amount of time finding the right song for the drive home.

person-170.name: Tolani Balogun
person-170.bio: I do heat relief work in Vegas. Getting a stubborn little plant to make it through August still makes my week.

person-171.name: Chinedu Nnamani
person-171.bio: I edit other people's sentences for a living. You're welcome to use bad grammar at my game table.

person-172.name: Ibrahim Musa
person-172.bio: I volunteer on flood cleanups around Lewisburg. Some nights I just want dry socks and a game with friends.

person-173.name: Tunde Adebayo
person-173.bio: I check buildings for leaks in Tampa. I've been known to use a board game box to demonstrate where the water gets in.

person-174.name: Emeka Okafor
person-174.bio: I map streams around Athens. I play pickup basketball with an old pair of shoes I should've replaced last season.

person-175.name: Femi Adeyemi
person-175.bio: I buy food for a hospital kitchen in Billings. The herbs I grow at home never make it past the first batch of pesto.

person-176.name: Obinna Ude
person-176.bio: I give bus tours in Memphis. I like hearing where visitors ended up eating after they took my suggestions.

person-177.name: Sadiq Lawal
person-177.bio: I lead a crew working in the woods near Spearfish. I'm still learning the winter sky, one constellation at a time.

person-178.name: Bayo Ogunleye
person-178.bio: I work on power lines in Charleston. I like hearing what a street looked like before the oldest poles went in.

person-179.name: Uche Nwankwo
person-179.bio: I help people get comfortable on their bikes. I'm still working on finding that same sweet spot with my golf swing.

person-180.name: Abdul Danjuma
person-180.bio: I transcribe court proceedings. At home my dog supplies most of the dialogue and I can finally leave the keyboard alone.

person-181.name: Wanjiku Muriuki
person-181.bio: I cook meals for a few folks around Sioux Falls. My favorite night in involves leftovers and a movie long enough for seconds.
person-181.occupation: Home cook and part-time meal prep owner

person-182.name: Achieng Odhiambo
person-182.bio: I direct community theater in Cleveland. I get just as nervous in the last minute of a basketball game as I do on opening night.

person-183.name: Njeri Kamau
person-183.bio: I sell my cheese at the farm market in Abingdon. I take a picture of the first wheel I cut from every batch.

person-184.name: Halima Abdi
person-184.bio: I help apprentices get settled into their first shops. In my own garden I'm the one who still needs somebody to show me how.

person-185.name: Nyambura Maina
person-185.bio: I work along the shoreline in Cape May. My paperbacks always end up with sand in the binding.

person-186.name: Atieno Onyango
person-186.bio: I used to work in hospital sterilization. These days I go out to weed one flower bed and come back two hours later.

person-187.name: Wairimu Karanja
person-187.bio: I'm learning to fix the big cranes at the port in Long Beach. I like having both feet on a trail on my days off.

person-188.name: Salma Hassan
person-188.bio: I schedule repairs for our electric co-op in Burlington. On Sundays I make a big pot of soup and send people home with leftovers.

person-189.name: Nafula Barasa
person-189.bio: I patch tents and jackets in Boone. There's probably a game of cards in one of the pockets of my own pack.

person-190.name: Wambui Njoroge
person-190.bio: I teach people to ride bikes through a Marquette winter. In February I start seeds indoors partly to remind myself there's a spring coming.

person-191.name: Brian Otieno
person-191.bio: I get horses and their people where they need to go. If a trailer latch rattles, I'll hear it for miles.

person-192.name: Kevin Mwangi
person-192.bio: I interpret at a hospital in Buffalo. I like an early tee time, especially when no one feels the need to keep score.

person-193.name: Abdi Mohamed
person-193.bio: I talk people through internet problems in Paintsville. My cat has interrupted enough calls to qualify as a coworker.

person-194.name: David Kiptoo
person-194.bio: I help families find their way around the school system in Aurora. I like old class photos, especially when someone remembers all the names.

person-195.name: Juma Omar
person-195.bio: I help clear storm debris in Cedar Key. If there's a hoop still standing at the end of the day, somebody usually has a ball.

person-196.name: Samuel Kariuki
person-196.bio: I work on diesel fleets in Peoria. I tell myself I have enough tools and then a neighbor shows up with a good project.

person-197.name: Peter Kibet
person-197.bio: I look after a neighborhood seed library. If you bring back seeds in a homemade envelope, I'll probably ask you how you folded it.

person-198.name: Mohammed Ali
person-198.bio: I work the desk at an inn in Saranac Lake. Want a walking route with a good story along the way? I've got a few.

person-199.name: Felix Ochieng
person-199.bio: I run a produce market on wheels. If you want to know what to do with an unfamiliar squash, the next person in line usually knows.

person-200.name: Joseph Wekesa
person-200.bio: I work at a school in Cedar Rapids. Movie night at my place starts as soon as the popcorn stops making noise.

person-201.name: Mariam Saad
person-201.bio: I spend a lot of time on foot in Albuquerque. I can give you directions by terrible curbs or by good places to eat.

person-202.name: Yasmin Adel
person-202.bio: I sew costumes in Providence. On clear nights I take my tea outside and try to spot something besides the Big Dipper.

person-203.name: Nour Youssef
person-203.bio: I work at a cargo yard in Tacoma. The folks at game night have finally stopped letting me arrange all the pieces before we start.

person-204.name: Salma Hamdy
person-204.bio: I used to rewire old houses in Birmingham. Now I like reading on the porch under a light I put in myself.

person-205.name: Nada Ibrahim
person-205.bio: I lead a conservation crew near Silver City. My favorite tools come back scratched up from somebody learning to use them.

person-206.name: Habiba Fawzi
person-206.bio: I coach high school ball. If a Saturday opens up, I'm happy to caddie, play, or just drive the golf cart.

person-207.name: Reem Mahmoud
person-207.bio: I teach welding at night in Albuquerque. The first time a student lifts their helmet and grins never gets old.

person-208.name: Farida Hossam
person-208.bio: I look after an apartment building in Charleston. Half the people I play basketball with started out asking me to fix a sink.

person-209.name: Hana Tarek
person-209.bio: I work with gauges and sensors around Tulsa. I keep a pile of broken things at home for the weekends I feel like tinkering.

person-210.name: Malak Hamed
person-210.bio: I drive a school bus in Presque Isle. On vacation I like taking a road where I have no idea what's around the bend.

person-211.name: Omar Khalil
person-211.bio: I look after equipment for a rec league. Somehow it’s always the left shin guard that gets left behind.

person-212.name: Karim Nassar
person-212.bio: I run a farmers market in Decorah. Once the last tent's packed away, I like to disappear into a game for a couple of hours.

person-213.name: Youssef Fahmy
person-213.bio: I spend weekdays in a shipping office. I keep a putter by my desk for those rare lunches when the phone stays quiet.

person-214.name: Hassan Farouk
person-214.bio: I work on fish habitat near Marquette. My pack usually has room for one more field guide than it really should.

person-215.name: Mostafa Gamal
person-215.bio: I run a food cart in New Haven. More than a few regulars have four legs and sit very politely by the wheel.

person-216.name: Ahmed Magdy
person-216.bio: I work with state records in Richmond. Old movies are my thing, especially if I can recognize one of the streets in them.

person-217.name: Amr Soliman
person-217.bio: I volunteer as an EMT. I like taking photos on quiet mornings when nobody needs me to hurry.

person-218.name: Khaled Fathy
person-218.bio: I repair ranch water systems around Alpine and help care for family. A neighbor who stops by for coffee gets offered a chair, even on a busy day.
person-218.occupation: Ranch water systems repairer and caregiver

person-219.name: Tarek Saeed
person-219.bio: I teach boxing in Tulsa. I've got a little telescope and always forget how long it takes to find anything besides the moon.

person-220.name: Yassin Hegazy
person-220.bio: I work at a water reuse plant in El Paso. I watch old monster movies and root for the person who spots the problem first.

person-221.name: Ananya Rao
person-221.bio: I drive equipment in an orchard. When harvest wraps up, I owe my friends about a month's worth of game nights.

person-222.name: Meera Nair
person-222.bio: I repair canoes in Hayward. My favorite paddle is the short one just after sunset when the first stars come out.

person-223.name: Kavya Kulkarni
person-223.bio: I take water samples around Milwaukee. I'm working on a photo album of the lake in every kind of weather.

person-224.name: Isha Menon
person-224.bio: I volunteer at trail races. I like taking pictures of the people cheering almost as much as the people running.

person-225.name: Neha Kapoor
person-225.bio: I do payroll for a restaurant. New Orleans is full of places where all I have to ask is “what was here before?” and I'm set for lunch.

person-226.name: Aditi Shah
person-226.bio: I'm a dentist in Putnam and an enthusiastic bench player on the basketball court. I'll set the screen if you take the shot.

person-227.name: Sana Qureshi
person-227.bio: I buy seafood in Cambridge. Ask me what's good this week or who's playing tonight. I can usually help with either.

person-228.name: Priya Das
person-228.bio: I wax skis in Anchorage. Most of my homemade jigs started as a piece of scrap wood I couldn't bring myself to toss.

person-229.name: Riya Banerjee
person-229.bio: I teach drums after school. A quiet night outside watching the sky makes a pretty good change of pace.

person-230.name: Nisha Iyer
person-230.bio: I keep books for contractors in Spearfish. At golf I prefer to let somebody else handle the numbers.

person-231.name: Arjun Mehta
person-231.bio: I mix sound for shows in Long Beach. I play pickup ball with people who have never once asked me to turn up a microphone.

person-232.name: Vikram Desai
person-232.bio: I work shifts at a wind farm near Cheyenne. If I've recorded the game, please let me get my boots off before you tell me the score.

person-233.name: Aditya Joshi
person-233.bio: I help survey floodplains around Greenville. My work boots and basketball shoes live in separate bags for a reason.

person-234.name: Rohan Malhotra
person-234.bio: I'm a middle school librarian. I check out cookbooks, bring them home and leave little floury fingerprints on the recipes I like.

person-235.name: Kabir Sethi
person-235.bio: I keep track of refrigerated shipments in Anchorage. Game day at my place starts whenever the last friend gets off shift.

person-236.name: Rahul Krishnan
person-236.bio: I guide hikes around Berlin. I can make a lunch break last a long time if there's a hoop and somebody has a ball.

person-237.name: Sameer Ansari
person-237.bio: I help folks work through benefits paperwork. I like trails with a bench and a view worth taking my time over.

person-238.name: Karan Bhat
person-238.bio: I work at a grain elevator in Devils Lake. The view from up there is what made me start carrying a camera.

person-239.name: Siddharth Pillai
person-239.bio: I test samples at a sugar mill in Thibodaux. I like volunteering at the kind of event where somebody hands me a job as soon as I arrive.

person-240.name: Nikhil Reddy
person-240.bio: I fix things in student apartments in Eugene. Once football season starts, I can usually hear the score through the open windows.

person-241.name: Maria Liza Ramos
person-241.bio: I dispatch trains in Galesburg. I come home to a dog who thinks every shift was personally too long.

person-242.name: Janelle Bautista
person-242.bio: I work the parts counter in Scottsbluff. During football season people bring in a bent part and stay for a full quarter.

person-243.name: Alyssa Villanueva
person-243.bio: I grow things with school kids in Hilo. We built a planter from scraps, and the kids are still prouder of the box than the beans.

person-244.name: Bianca Panganiban
person-244.bio: I keep the books for a community orchestra. My favorite camping spot is one where I don't have to reserve anything in advance.

person-245.name: Rina Mercado
person-245.bio: I work on irrigation canals around Scottsbluff. I like a late pickup game when it's finally cool enough to run.

person-246.name: Paula Reyes
person-246.bio: I keep track of rental cars in St. Louis. Somehow in racing games I'm always the one who returns the car wrecked.

person-247.name: Cristina Mendoza
person-247.bio: I teach brass in New Orleans. My porch has just enough room for a chair, a horn and more pots of herbs than I intended.

person-248.name: Joanna Navarro
person-248.bio: I work on a ferry out of Portland. I mark my place in my book with old tickets until they fall out.

person-249.name: Camille Dizon
person-249.bio: I take wedding pictures in Newark. I'm happy to walk the golf course with friends even when my swing stays home.

person-250.name: Patricia Salazar
person-250.bio: I receive parts at the rail shop in Winslow. Lately I've been trying to coax tomatoes out of a windy corner of the yard.

person-251.name: Miguel Dela Cruz
person-251.bio: I retired from helping people sort out insurance claims. These days the toughest calls I make are from the couch during basketball games.

person-252.name: Rafael Santos
person-252.bio: I make maple syrup in St. Johnsbury. My dog comes along to check the lines and takes full credit for the walk.

person-253.name: Paolo Manalo
person-253.bio: I do community health work in Memphis. I've never been sorry I stayed for one more song.

person-254.name: Angelo Reyes
person-254.bio: I coordinate clinical studies in Durham. My favorite notification on my phone tells me when the space station is about to pass overhead.

person-255.name: Luis Agustin
person-255.bio: I grow seed potatoes in Presque Isle. Long winter evenings are what got our weekly card game started.

person-256.name: Jose Carlo Mariano
person-256.bio: I work at a neighborhood credit union in Cleveland. I can spend a whole Sunday with a football game on the radio and something in the oven.

person-257.name: Adrian Lim
person-257.bio: I help run an adaptive canoe program in Honolulu. On rainy afternoons I'll take a good book almost anywhere.

person-258.name: Joshua Garcia
person-258.bio: I keep score for baseball on the radio in Peoria. When I travel, I try to catch a game and bring home a paper scorecard.

person-259.name: Marco Velasco
person-259.bio: I take care of river access spots near Salida. I like hearing what the old-timers called each bend before there were signs.

person-260.name: Nico Valdez
person-260.bio: I run a hospital laundry crew in Bethel. I'm always looking for short stories I can finish over lunch.

person-261.name: Aoi Fujimoto
person-261.bio: I work with young climbers in Salt Lake City. I've been building a gear rack at home for so long it practically counts as a hobby.

person-262.name: Yui Hasegawa
person-262.bio: I work the mountain roads around Boone. The dog knows a day off by which boots I put on.

person-263.name: Misaki Watanabe
person-263.bio: I service hotel elevators in Vegas. On nights when I have the kitchen to myself I'll make fresh noodles and leave flour everywhere.

person-264.name: Sakura Tanaka
person-264.bio: I organize arts programs for kids in Buffalo. I'll take any excuse to haul the paint and paper outside.

person-265.name: Hina Matsumoto
person-265.bio: I check on streams around Saranac Lake. After a cold morning out there, all I want is my own kitchen and a pot of stew.

person-266.name: Rin Shimizu
person-266.bio: I cut hair in Jackson. If you're putting together a game night, I'll bring the dominoes.

person-267.name: Akari Sato
person-267.bio: I work at a truck scale near Cheyenne. I like a long song for the drive in and a loud one for the drive home.

person-268.name: Hana Kimura
person-268.bio: I work nights in radiology. My neighbors are used to seeing me water the garden at breakfast in my scrubs.

person-269.name: Nanami Okada
person-269.bio: I work in a college dining hall in Charleston. I like taking pictures of campus before the first students roll in for coffee.

person-270.name: Mio Inoue
person-270.bio: I manage a grocery department in Berlin. On vacation I always end up in somebody else's grocery store to see what they carry.

person-271.name: Haruto Nakajima
person-271.bio: I buy for a grocery co-op in Duluth. At board game night I'm usually responsible for the snacks, and I take requests.

person-272.name: Ren Kobayashi
person-272.bio: I help families enroll their kids in school. My idea of a good weekend is a kitchen full of people folding something for dinner.

person-273.name: Yuta Suzuki
person-273.bio: I volunteer with a land trust in Detroit. I like walking a golf course with friends, even when the golf itself goes badly.

person-274.name: Sota Nakamura
person-274.bio: I help keep the floodwall in shape in Madison. My favorite home repairs are the ones I can finish before the hardware store closes.

person-275.name: Hiroto Hayashi
person-275.bio: I run an after-school chess group in Charleston. I'll happily trade you a beginner opening for a good seat at the football game.

person-276.name: Kaito Ishikawa
person-276.bio: I help renters in Boone. I cook beans a different way almost every week and rarely write down which one worked.

person-277.name: Daiki Mori
person-277.bio: I work with tenants in Manchester. My library holds all seem to arrive on the same afternoon.

person-278.name: Riku Yamamoto
person-278.bio: I own a little comic shop in Tacoma. Tell me the last thing you stayed up reading and I'll find you another one.

person-279.name: Shun Ogawa
person-279.bio: I answer the intake phone at legal aid in Louisville. I spend some evenings on the back step shelling peas or watching them grow.

person-280.name: Yuki Abe
person-280.bio: I record musicians in Detroit. I love helping somebody make the first track they feel brave enough to play for their friends.

person-281.name: Ji-eun Park
person-281.bio: I grade roads near Pinedale. Once I'm home, I like a video game where the entire point is to drive off-road.

person-282.name: Seo-yeon Kim
person-282.bio: I cover the statehouse for radio. By the time I get home, checking what's come up in the garden is about my speed.

person-283.name: Hye-jin Lee
person-283.bio: I install exhibits in North Adams. I like the part of a planetarium show where the room goes quiet just before the stars appear.

person-284.name: Ha-yun Choi
person-284.bio: I run an outdoor preschool in Sandpoint. I keep an emergency picture book in a plastic bag for rainy afternoons.

person-285.name: Su-bin Han
person-285.bio: I help get rentals cleaned up around Cedar Key. If you find an old postcard of the island, I'd love to see it.

person-286.name: Ye-jin Kang
person-286.bio: I'm learning the meat trade in Burns. I like books with short chapters that I can finish on a break.

person-287.name: Min-seo Jung
person-287.bio: I cater weddings in Madison. At home I eat standing over the stove more often than anyone who owns this many plates should.

person-288.name: Yu-na Song
person-288.bio: I make animations in Albuquerque. Give me a stack of sticky notes and I'll probably make something walk across your desk.

person-289.name: Da-eun Yoon
person-289.bio: I volunteer with local history in Devils Lake. I collect old football programs and try to put names to the team photos.

person-290.name: Hye-won Lim
person-290.bio: I schedule maintenance at a sawmill in Elkins. At game night I like taking my turn without having to check the calendar first.

person-291.name: Min-jun Lee
person-291.bio: I sell books in Cape May. Dogs are welcome to browse, though so far their taste runs mostly to the biscuit tin.

person-292.name: Ji-ho Kim
person-292.bio: I work at a bank in Westerly. I'm one of those people who listens to the postgame show all the way through.

person-293.name: Hyun-woo Park
person-293.bio: I show people the night sky around Tucson. My dog gets very excited when the telescope comes out because it means we're going outside.

person-294.name: Seung-min Choi
person-294.bio: I help students with distance classes in Ely. I'm trying to grow herbs on a windowsill that gets exactly one good patch of sun.

person-295.name: Jun-seo Kang
person-295.bio: I fix bike-share bikes in Burlington. The first thing I do in a new city is look for a bike and a route by the water.

person-296.name: Jae-hyun Song
person-296.bio: I travel between schools as a speech therapist. I carry a box of games that's held together by optimism and packing tape.

person-297.name: Do-yun Han
person-297.bio: I bring a telescope to community nights in Price. By daylight I'm usually out looking for the seedlings I forgot to label.

person-298.name: Tae-hyun Shin
person-298.bio: I help run park programs in Peoria. If we've got a shelter and a grill, I can usually talk a few people into staying for lunch.

person-299.name: Hyun-jin Yoon
person-299.bio: I help students in a college lab in New Haven. There's a moon map above my desk that gets more questions than anything else there.

person-300.name: Jin-woo Kwon
person-300.bio: I mentor young people in Newark. I still love the look on someone's face the first time they see Saturn through a telescope.
